newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent late-Nov unleaded prices plunge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent late-Nov unleaded prices plunge.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent late-November spot unleaded gasoline basis "collapsed" on Tuesday, falling victim to stepped up production in the region, traders said.
A correction in the Group Three market rippled through Chicago, easing spot unleaded prices by up to two cents a gallon on late-November barrels and weakening first-cycle December basis.
"Everything just collapsed," one trader said, citing higher production from regional refineries and perceptions of ample gasoline supplies in the Midwest.

Midwest refineries were operating at 98 percent of rated capacity after Clark Refining and Marketing restarted a fluid catalytic cracker at its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery. Traders will be closely watching production estimates due out late in the day to see if output has remained at that blistering pace.

Chicago unleaded for late-November deliveries fell to even to 0.25 cent a gallon below NYMEX December unleaded. First-cycle December barrels were talked 2.0/2.25 cents over January unleaded futures, with later deliveries 0.75/0.50 cent under the print.
Group Three unleaded gasoline was heard done as high as 2.0 cents a gallon over the print, but in late-morning discussion weakened to bids even with the print.

Group Three low sulphur diesel was steady at bids 2.25 cents a gallon under the print, and high sulphur eased to 3.0 cents a gallon under the print on talk of deliveries due in December's first cycle.
Chicago low sulphur diesel remained bid even with the print, and high sulphur was talked 0.75 cent under the print.
